text:
Trevor Zegras is in the hardest stretch of his second Flyers season. He has one goal and two points in his last ten games, his minutes are down 1:19 a night over that run, and in Ottawa on Nov. 19 he played 12:48. He told PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor that a third-period roughing penalty was why: "I just didn't love the hit on Jamie, & they had just scored. Obviously I'm not trying to take one there." Rick Tocchet's view, per O'Connor: "I think that he needs a little bit more predictability in his game."

The five-on-five numbers help explain the message. Philadelphia gets only 38% of the expected goals with him on, 8.7 points worse than without him. That's a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had his team creating more with him on (94th percentile of forwards).

There's bad luck in it too. He has 5 goals on 7.4 expected, and the Flyers have scored 7.6 fewer goals than expected with him out there, so we flag him as due. O'Connor saw the good version in Montreal on Nov. 21: gaining the zone through three defenders and finding Matvei Michkov as the trailer.
